ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, two sufficiently long parallel metal rails are spaced at a distance of $L=0.5\mathrm{m}$, with an inclination angle of $\theta{=}30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal plane. They are placed in a uniform magnetic field with a magnetic induction strength of $B=0.2\mathrm{T}$, directed vertically upward relative to the plane of the rails. The conductor rods $a$ and $b$ on the rails have masses of $m_a=0.3\mathrm{kg}$ and $m_b=0.1\mathrm{kg}$, respectively, and each has a resistance of $R=0.1\Omega$. The rods $a$ and $b$ are released from rest, and a constant force $F$ of magnitude 2N is applied to rod $a$ along the direction parallel to the rails, pulling it upward. The rails are smooth, and their resistance is negligible. During the motion, the two rods remain perpendicular to the rails and maintain good contact. The gravitational acceleration is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. It is known that when the Joule heat generated in rod $a$ is $Q_{a}=0.12\mathrm{J}$, its velocity is $v_a=1.0\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.

1. At this moment, the speed magnitude of rod $b$.
2. At this moment, the magnitude of the acceleration of rod $b$
3. The time it takes for rod $a$ to accelerate from rest to a speed of $1.0\mathrm{m/s}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two sufficiently long parallel metal guide rails, the whole is inclined relative to the horizontal dashed line, and the included angle is marked as θ; two conducting rods a and b span between the two rails and are perpendicular to the guide rails, with a located on the uphill side of b. In the figure, the arrow of F acts on rod a along the uphill direction of the guide rails; the arrow of B indicates that the magnetic field is upward relative to the plane of the guide rails. Reasoning: Take the uphill direction along the guide rails as positive. It is known that L=0.5 m, B=0.2 T, R=0.1 Ω, m_a=0.3 kg, m_b=0.1 kg, θ=30°, F=2 N, g=10 m/s^2. 1. Because F=(m_a+m_b)g sinθ=(0.3+0.1)×10×0.5=2 N, the resultant external force of the two-rod system along the direction of the guide rails is zero; the magnetic forces on the two rods are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, and the system is initially at rest, so momentum is conserved: m_a v_a+m_b v_b=0. When v_a=1.0 m/s, v_b=-(m_a/m_b)v_a=-(0.3/0.1)×1=-3 m/s, that is, rod b moves along the downhill direction, with a speed of 3 m/s. 2. At this time the relative velocity u=v_a-v_b=1-(-3)=4 m/s. The total resistance of the loop is 2R=0.2 Ω, and the current I=BLu/(2R)=0.2×0.5×4/0.2=2 A. The magnitude of the magnetic force on rod b is f=BIL=0.2×2×0.5=0.2 N, and the direction is uphill. The component of the gravity of rod b along the inclined plane is m_b g sinθ=0.1×10×0.5=0.5 N, so m_b a_b=f-m_b g sinθ=0.2-0.5=-0.3 N, therefore a_b=-3 m/s^2, with magnitude 3 m/s^2. 3. According to the specified sign-axis Newton equation route, from the momentum relation there is v_b=-(m_a/m_b)v_a=-3v_a. The instantaneous equation of rod a can be written as m_a dv_a/dt=F-m_a g sinθ-[B^2L^2/(2R)](v_a-v_b), where B^2L^2/(2R)=0.05, therefore 0.3 dv_a/dt=0.5-0.2v_a. Direct integration to v_a=1 m/s gives t approximately 0.77 s. If at the same time the problem-given Joule heat already produced by rod a at that moment, Q_a=0.12 J, is used to determine the displacement at this moment, the standard value can be obtained: total Joule heat Q=2Q_a=0.24 J, kinetic energy increment ΔK=0.5×0.3×1^2+0.5×0.1×3^2=0.6 J. Let the uphill displacement of rod a be s, then from the integrated momentum relation s_b=-3s, the total work done by gravity on the two rods cancels mutually, and the work done by the external force F is Fs=ΔK+Q=0.84 J, hence s=0.42 m. Integrating the Newton equation of rod a: m_a v_a=(F-m_a g sinθ)t-[B^2L^2/(2R)](s-s_b). Here s-s_b=0.42-(-1.26)=1.68 m, and the magnetic-force impulse is 0.05×1.68=0.084 N·s, so 0.3=0.5t-0.084, giving t=0.768 s. Final answer: The speed of rod b is 3 m/s; the magnitude of the acceleration of rod b is 3 m/s^2; the time for rod a to accelerate from rest to 1.0 m/s is 0.768 s.
